subject: asp-es
title: ASP.ES.------SPT.D.
description: Diagram in AF(D)-12 (Affinity Dynamics, Level One), first of two on book p84, paired with v2-p84-2. Opens Braxton's transfer-cycles analysis: 'the concept of transfer cycles can be viewed with respect to the nature underlying how information is passed through various time zones and culture groups.' (C)ASP-ES (the concept of aspect essence) is crossed with SPT-D (spectacle dynamics): the question is what aspect-essence produces when crossed with spectacle-dynamics — aspect-essence being the perceptual-extraction layer through which transfer-cycles operate, spectacle-dynamics being what disrupts that layer in the western context. (R)TM (the reality of time) sits centrally between subject and partner. AFN (affinity) hangs on the upper-right margin via a *dashed* edge from SPT-D — the only conditional relation, marking that affinity's link to spectacle-dynamics is uncertain (spectacle attempts to redirect affinity but does not deterministically capture it). S-ST (source-state) anchors the left margin. ALT-D (alternative dynamics) hangs on the right output. PROG-CONT (progressional continuance) sits lower-center between the two upper output chains. CRTF-D (creative-dynamic) anchors the lower-center. Structural argument: aspect-essence crossed with spectacle-dynamics is mediated by the reality-of-time as central hub, with source-state and creative-dynamic as upstreams. The dashed AFN edge is load-bearing: it exposes Braxton's structural insight that affinity is *not* automatically captured by spectacle — there is structural slack in that edge, which is where transfer-cycles can be honestly read. The diagram is the case that aspect-essence (perception of essence-traits) and spectacle-dynamics are in productive tension only when time-reality, source-state, and creative-dynamic are all live upstreams.
